scorecard.note: Correct the total USPS mail volume figure to match official data; the current 109 billion claim appears inaccurate.

storyboard.ears: Fewer letters made mailing one more expensive, not cheaper.
USPS mail fell to 109 billion pieces, leaving the network with nearly half its former traffic.
storyboard.eyes: substance: white paper envelopes; cause: Data grips each cart's handle and rolls the letters out of the truck, cart after cart
storyboard.evidence: Postal Regulatory Commission (PRC) | Total USPS mail volume | https://www.prc.gov/state-of-the-postal-service | 2026-10-16

storyboard.ears: First-Class Mail fell to 46 billion pieces, showing letters disappeared fastest.
storyboard.eyes: substance: white paper letters; cause: Data stamps each letter and sends it to the mail sack, and the pigeonholes empty
storyboard.evidence: United States Postal Service (USPS) | First-Class Mail volume | https://about.usps.com/who/profile/history/pdf/first-class-mail-since-1926.pdf | 2026-10-16

storyboard.ears: A stamp reached 68 cents, because shrinking volume did not shrink the nationwide delivery network.
storyboard.evidence: United States Postal Service (USPS) | Price of a First-Class stamp | https://about.usps.com/newsroom/service-alerts/postal-facts.htm | 2026-10-16

storyboard.ears: Every mailbox costs money to reach, even when fewer letters help fund the trip.
